### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/runtime.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/runtime.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **14** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e71ef829f28aeb17a65390f9487b37c49dc8449` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ca061756b1713590e7a86b86265533ec362d5582` — the merge of head `15faf1da07c5b4811bb16eb31444c5ba0651106b` into base `9e71ef829f28aeb17a65390f9487b37c49dc8449`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ca061756b1713590e7a86b86265533ec362d5582 && git checkout ca061756b1713590e7a86b86265533ec362d5582
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9e71ef829f28aeb17a65390f9487b37c49dc8449 15faf1da07c5b4811bb16eb31444c5ba0651106b && git checkout -B drift-repro 9e71ef829f28aeb17a65390f9487b37c49dc8449 && git merge --no-ff 15faf1da07c5b4811bb16eb31444c5ba0651106b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e71ef829f28aeb17a65390f9487b37c49dc8449
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9e71ef829f28aeb17a65390f9487b37c49dc8449` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 review (L1-d) · 2026-11-17T21:07Z

L1: REWORK
Head-sha: `f34867b93d61caf5b11ae77e7733369e7b6a8f16`

Read against claim 6957893698, amendment 6960995968 (the seat's ruling B, 21:04Z) and os-dev report 6960939459 on #34884.
- **Size:** 18 files, +548/-6.
- **Not governed:** 0 of 18 paths on the register, 554 lines.
- **CI at this head:** still running (17 success, 10 skipped, 39 in progress, 0 failed).
- **Claim surface:** the 18 files are inside the original claim: lint and its rule ripples (index, rule-explanations, the runtime roster pin, and the four "rules (71)" transcript lines), the sandbox runner and its test, the authoring and error-catalog docs, and the changeset.

The code holds. The REWORK is only because the seat's ruling B came after this head and is not in it yet.

### What holds
- **Closing keyword.** It fixes the card's two asks.
  - Author time: `action-body-does-not-compile` (gating, error) compiles each L2 `type: 'script'` action body inside `actionBodyFunctionExpression(source)`, which is `(async (input, ctx) => { SOURCE })`. It compiles with `node:vm` `Script` (falling back to `new Function`, or no verdict when the host refuses to compile at all). It never runs the body: a source that closes the wrapper early only compiles.
  - The rule runs on validate, build, lint and verify, and at the `action` and `object` publish doors, charging a write only with the bodies it adds.
  - The card's `const input = ctx.input || {}` is refused byte for byte. The finding gives line 1 and a hint naming the wrapper parameter.
- **One wrapper.** The QuickJS runner now builds its wrapper from the same `actionBodyFunctionExpression`, imported through `@objectstack/lint/runtime`. That entry is dependency-free and runtime already depends on lint. The wrapper text is byte-identical to before. The ⛔ comments on both sides forbid a second spelling.
- **The engine difference is handled honestly.** Only a host-refused regular-expression literal is a `warning` (V8 refuses duplicate named groups, QuickJS runs them, and both were measured over a 36-body probe). Syntax the host accepts but QuickJS does not becomes a missed finding, never a false one.
- **Run time.**
  - An `evalCode` `SyntaxError` on an action is a compile failure: the async arrow cannot throw synchronously, so anything the body throws crosses `__error` instead. It now answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` with a sentence naming the action and the compiler's reason (240 characters at most), where it used to answer the bare "Internal server error".
  - A runtime crash, including a `JSON.parse` `SyntaxError`, keeps the sanitised 500, and that is pinned.
  - No code is declared, so the doors relay the sentence.
- **Ablations.** Neutering the lint check turns 9 of 14 red. Disabling the runtime compile branch turns both compile pins red. Both were restored by blob.
- **Live.** validate, build and verify exit 1 naming the rule. REST and MCP answer with the naming sentence. Meta PUT gives 422 `INVALID_METADATA` and a control body gives 200. The examples app-todo, app-crm and app-multi-package have 0 hits.
- **Dogfood.** The battery passed at `1190befe` (the two later commits touch only one runtime test the battery does not read).

### Must-fix
- **M1: the seat's ruling B is not in this head.** Amendment 6960995968 moves `Metadata-protocol` from `none` to `narrowed`. It requires an ADR-0087 semantic migration entry under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/` (shaped like `18.lookup-filter-record-path-multi-valued-refused.ts`, plus whatever the roster requires) and a `@objectstack/spec` line in the changeset. At this head the changeset still says `Metadata-protocol: none` with the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, and nothing under `packages/spec` changes. Please push the entry and the changeset update, and re-run the ADR-0087 registration gate and `changeset-no-major`. I'll do a delta read on that head.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1: There is a known text conflict with #34791 on the four "author-time rules (70 → 71)" transcript lines, since both add a rule. Whichever lands second bumps to 72 on its merge-forward. `check:docs-transcript-drift` will name it if anyone forgets.
- N2: Hook and job bodies (the `(async (ctx) => …)` wrapper) stay out, per the seat, and triage files the follow-up. The changeset says "Hook and job bodies are unchanged."
- N3: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` will need the contract-review-tier review the claim names before the queue.

Landing: not governed. After M1 come the L1-d delta, the seat's narrowing review, and fully green CI on the final head. Then area o3-C lands it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `15faf1da07c5b4811bb16eb31444c5ba0651106b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.action-body-does-not-compile-refused.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-action-body-compiles.ts, packages/lint/src/action-body-wrapper.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts

Read for this record: card #34884 (body and all six comments, the 21:04Z ruling B as carried by claim amendment 6960995968), PR #34980 (body, 20 files, net diff against merge base `9e71ef829f`), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `collectActionBodies` (`validate-action-body-writes.ts`), `runtime-gate.ts` (snapshot set and differential), `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` (D1 to D4), `body-runner.ts` (`actionBodyRunnerFactory`), `registry-object-registration.ts` (`attachBoundActions`), `SemanticMigration` in `migrations/types.ts`, the precedent entry `18.lookup-filter-record-path-multi-valued-refused.ts`, `.changeset/config.json`.

Check-runs on the head: every completed run is `success` or `skipped` except one `Check Changeset` `failure` completed 22:24:02Z; two later `Check Changeset` runs on the same head (22:26:57Z and 23:21:44Z) are `success`, so the failure is superseded. Test Core 10/10 shards, Test UI 16/16 shards, TypeScript Type Check, Lint and Repo Gates, Build Core, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness and Governed Surface Queue Guard are `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, CLI doors (narrowed, right).** An action with `type: 'script'` (or no `type`, the schema default) and `body.language: 'js'` whose `body.source` does not compile as `(async (input, ctx) => { SOURCE })` is refused at `error` by `os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` (`commands: ALL`, `tier: 'gating'`). The walk is `collectActionBodies`: `stack.actions[]` and `stack.objects[].actions[]`, a merged action once. This is the population the runtime binds: `actionBodyRunnerFactory` binds a body only for `type ?? 'script'` equal to `script`, and the runner wraps only an L2 body. Expression bodies, non-script actions, hooks and jobs are not walked. Right, and exactly the entry's `surface`.
- **Accept-set, publish door (narrowed, right).** `runtimeTypes: ['action', 'object']`. `object_extension` is correctly absent: `ObjectExtensionSchema` refuses `actions` by guidance, so no third write type carries an action body. The gate judges `state: 'active'` only (D1), so a draft save of such a body is still admitted and its publish is refused, the same posture as every other door rule and the entry's "saved or published" wording, which is the precedent's.
- **Accept-set, object write carrying a stored body unchanged (narrowed, right as declared, stated here because the PR's account is narrower than the tree).** The differential is candidate minus a baseline that drops the written item, and the stored self's own findings never cancel (`runtime-gate.ts`, `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshotSet`). So an `object` publish that carries a non-compiling inline body is refused whether or not this write changed that body, including a body stored before the rule and a write-back of a served read that attached it (`attachBoundActions`). The pinned case "an unrelated write is not charged" covers a write of ANOTHER object only. This is the entry's declared surface ("PUT /api/v1/meta/object/NAME with inline actions") and the same posture every gating object rule has at this door (D4: new writes are blocked, stored rows keep being read, `OS_ALLOW_UNLINTED_METADATA_WRITES=1` for a migration window). See N1.
- **Advisory arm (right).** A host `SyntaxError` whose sentence opens `Invalid regular expression` is `warning`, never a refusal. This is the one measured place where a host refusal does not predict a QuickJS refusal, and the entry, the explanation and the docs all say it.
- **No verdict (right direction).** A host that will not compile at all, or that throws anything other than a `SyntaxError`, yields no finding. On Node 22.0 to 22.2 (inside `engines`, before `process.getBuiltinModule`) the `Function` fallback compiles the text as a function body, which accepts strictly more than a script (`new.target`, a `return` after an early close), so it can miss a finding and cannot invent one.
- **Engine disagreement (accepted on the dev's measurement).** The rule's verdict is the host engine's, the runtime's is QuickJS. Host accepts and QuickJS refuses: a missed finding, answered at run time by the naming 500. Host refuses and QuickJS accepts outside regular expressions: a false refusal. I found no realistic case by reading (redeclarations, grammar, strict-mode and `new.target` errors are early errors in both), and the 36-body probe found none; it is a measured claim, not a proof, and read-only I did not re-run it.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/lint` (additive, right).** `.` gains `validateActionBodyCompiles`, `hostCompileFailure`, `ACTION_BODY_DOES_NOT_COMPILE`, `ACTION_BODY_PARAMETERS`, `actionBodyFunctionExpression` and the types `ActionBodyCompileFinding`, `HostCompileFailure`; `./runtime` gains `actionBodyFunctionExpression` only. `action-body-wrapper.ts` has no imports, so the kernel-safe entry gains no dependency. The changeset names every one.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec` (additive, right).** One semantic entry in the 18 step; the registry is generated and uncommitted, so no other spec file moves.
- **Run-time answer, `@objectstack/runtime` (changed, right).** For `origin.kind === 'action'` only, an `evalCode` error named `SyntaxError` becomes `SandboxError(status 500, no code)` with operator line `action 'NAME' does not compile: …` and a caller sentence; REST answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` with that sentence (pinned through the real `/actions` door). Hook and job bodies keep `threw:` and the sanitised answer. The wrapper text the runner evaluates is byte-identical to before (`(async (input, ctx) => { ${source} })`).

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — present on the PR body and in the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and the marker `adr-0087: registered action-body-does-not-compile-refused` in both places the gates read.

`@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/runtime` patch. Right: lint publishes new exports and a new gating rule, spec publishes a new registry entry, runtime changes one error answer and imports an existing dependency's new export, with no new export of its own. All three sit in the one `fixed` group, so the release level is the group's minor. It matches both precedents the PR cites (`34378`, `33435`: lint minor, spec minor, narrowing under `!` with no major), and `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head (22:26:57Z and 23:21:44Z; the 22:24:02Z failure predates the body patch).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1, Metadata-protocol none or narrowed.** Answered by the seat's ruling B; in this head (entry, changeset line, marker). Closed.
- **Open question 2, hook and job bodies.** Answered: out of this PR. The tree agrees (the rule walks actions only, the runner's new branch is gated on `kind === 'action'`). The follow-up card is reported "noted, not filed" in both dev reports: owed by the seat or triage, not by this head.
- **Open question 3, the object door.** Answered: keep it. I agree. An object write is the second place a body is published and `object_extension` cannot carry one, so `['action', 'object']` is the whole set. Its cost is the third bullet of ① and N1.
- **Skills-docs follow-up** on `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md`: declared on the PR body and the changeset, not filed. Owed by the seat.
- **No user-text catalog for the rule.** Accepted: the door renders the finding's `message` and `hint`, which name the action, the compiler's sentence and the line.
- **Text conflict with #34791** on the rule-count transcript lines and the `validating-metadata.mdx` table: a landing-order matter for the seat; `check:docs-transcript-drift` names it if missed.
- **Docs drift check** listed `validating-metadata.mdx`; the head adds the rule's row there.
- **SQL push-down.** Not applicable: the diff reads no data, materialises no ids and joins nothing.
- **Security.** The author-time check compiles untrusted source on the host and never runs it: `new vm.Script` compiles only, the `Function` fallback constructs and discards, and the early-close case is pinned as not executing. The run-time sentence relays the first line of QuickJS's compile error, capped at 240 characters; a compile error carries no record data.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.action-body-does-not-compile-refused.ts` (hits).** Read against the ruling, the precedent entry and its first consumer, the rule.

- `surface`: the two paths are the paths `collectActionBodies` emits (`actions[N].body.source`, `objects[N].actions[N].body.source`); "type script whose body.language is js" is its filter; the doors named are the gate's (item save, object save, `publish-drafts`, per-item publish) and the three commands. Holds.
- `replacement`: `var input = …` compiles (pinned); `422 INVALID_METADATA` is the gate's envelope (D3); the regular-expression sentence is the code's `warning` arm. Holds.
- `reason`: the parse check's different wrapper is pinned by the test that compiles the card's body inside `async function __body(ctx)`; "from the same function" is true of `quickjs-runner.ts`; "Hook and job bodies … are not judged" is true; "no stored row changes shape" is true, since nothing is converted and stored rows keep being read. Holds.
- `acceptanceCriteria`: checkable by an author with a CLI (`os validate` / `os build`) and by a runtime author (the PUT and the action run). Holds.
- Upgrade of an existing package, which the brief asks about: a built artifact holding such a body still boots and installs (the gate judges writes, not reads; the dev booted a pre-rule artifact), its runs answer the naming 500 where they answered the opaque one, `os build` of the source now exits 1 until the body is fixed, and any publish that carries the body is refused. The entry states the build and publish halves and not the "still loads, now answers naming itself" half; the changeset does. See N2.

**`validate-action-body-compiles.ts`.** Agrees with the entry. Line N of the finding is line N of `body.source` because the wrapper keeps the source on its first line. The parameter hint fires only for `input` / `ctx`. Tried to break it: a body that closes the wrapper early compiles and does not execute (pinned); a non-`SyntaxError` from the host is no verdict; a redeclaration through `var` or a nested function is admitted, as QuickJS admits it. See N3 and N4.

**`action-body-wrapper.ts`, `index.ts`, `runtime.ts`.** One spelling, no imports, exported on both entries as the changeset says. Agrees.

**`authoring-rules.ts`.** `gating` on all three commands, `CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `['action', 'object']`. Agrees with the entry and the docs row. The rule reaches the kernel path without `typescript` / `sucrase` (its only sibling import is the dependency-free walk), which is why it may cross where the other body rules may not. See N1.

**`rule-explanations.ts`.** Agrees with the module and the runner, including the sentence that host-accepted syntax QuickJS refuses is answered at run time.

**`quickjs-runner.ts`.** The branch is gated on the action kind and on the error's `name`; the control case (a `SyntaxError` thrown by `JSON.parse` while running) stays a sanitised crash and is pinned. The sentence is in the caller's language: it names the action, says it cannot run, gives the compiler's reason and says who must act. The card asked for "a 4xx/5xx with a code, never a bare Internal server error": the answer is `500` with the status's own `INTERNAL_ERROR` and a naming message, so a caller tells a compile failure from a crash by the message, not by the code; the runner's comment gives the reason no code is declared (a declared 5xx code would withhold the sentence), and the door test pins the outcome. Accepted. See N5.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (none moves correctness or the contract; none is owed on this head):

- N1 (nit) — `authoring-rules.ts`, the registration comment: "the differential charges a write only with the bodies it adds" is narrower than the code. A write is charged with every non-compiling body the written item CARRIES, changed or not; only another entry's findings cancel. The behaviour is the declared one; the sentence is not. Left as an accepted deviation, or corrected in a later touch of the file.
- N2 (nit) — the entry does not say that an already deployed body keeps loading and now answers a 500 naming itself, nor that an object publish is refused while it carries such a body unchanged; the changeset and the docs say the first. A sentence in `reason` would carry both into the upgrade guide.
- N3 (nit) — `validate-action-body-compiles.ts`: V8 reports an unterminated regular-expression literal as `Invalid regular expression: missing /`, which takes the `warning` arm although both engines refuse it. A missed refusal inside the declared advisory arm, answered at run time.
- N4 (nit) — the same module's header says the run-time answer is "a coded `500`"; the runner declares no code and says so. One of the two sentences should match the other.
- N5 (nit) — `isCompileFailure`'s comment says a `SyntaxError` at `evalCode` is always the compiler's. A body that closes the wrapper early and calls something synchronously in the argument list can throw one while running, and it would be answered with the naming sentence. Only a body written to escape the wrapper does this, and its author can already return any text as the action's result.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34884-action-body-compile`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**VERDICT: PASS**
